blocks.content:
• Article 79 – Structure of Parliament
• Lok Sabha – House of the People
• Rajya Sabha – Permanent House
• Money Bill – Article 110
• Joint sitting – Article 108
• Anti-Defection Law – 52nd Amendment (1985)
• Speaker certifies Money Bill

items: The Speaker holds exclusive power to certify whether a bill is a Money Bill under Article 110.
Joint sitting of Parliament is convened under Article 108.
Anti-Defection Law is associated with the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1985.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 79 prescribes the official structure of the Parliament of India.
Lok Sabha functions as the House of the People, whereas Rajya Sabha is the Permanent House.
Money Bill provisions are laid down in Article 110, and its certification authority rests solely with the Speaker.
Article 108 governs the provision for a Joint sitting of Parliament.
The Anti-Defection Law was introduced through the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
